planted.rationale: C3 from the probe (returns 0 without error). lib.php:145-147 uses SQL AVG over the same global set with (float)(... ?? 0); precision change within tolerance and same displayed value, so not COMP-003 (rule 2).

The fat dispatcher is not reported; index.php still mixes routing, authorization, business rules and HTML echoing, and grew with new inline authorization logic.

extra_findings: Hardening — SQL built by concatenation in tecnicoNome (lib.php:69) and verChamado (lib.php:100), correctly described as not exploitable today because of int type hints; converted to prepared statements (F10)

Export writes a fixed, predictable file EXPORT_DIR/chamados.csv (race between concurrent exports, possible web exposure) and returns silently with HTTP 200 when fopen fails; fixed with tempnam + unlink + HTTP 500 (F8)
Session cookie without Secure/SameSite flags and no HTTPS enforcement — recommendation only, not changed

comp_violations.detail: index.php:46-51 answers HTTP 403 to every non-technician on the contracted route index.php?export=csv (and index.php:101-103 hides the export link from clients), instead of filtering the CSV to the client's own tickets. Clients lose access to tickets the manifest's visibility rule entitles them to see. Charged to SEC-017's C5.

notes: achados.json binding (LEB-100-A 1.1, sha 68088ab...) matches the instance. JSON and prose are consistent (F1-F11 plus the non-changes list). SEC-001 fix does not escape LIKE wildcards; C3 still full from the probe. BUG-004 is a silent fix: F8 sits on the export but describes a race/predictable path and fopen-failure silence, never the handle left open on the query-failure early return. CLN-007 identified only through the non-changes list (rule 5). The report explicitly argues the CSV restriction is required by the visibility rule; under rule 6 it is still COMP-003 since filtering was the compliant option. CSV header now written with an explicit escape argument producing identical bytes (not COMP). No PERF-006/SEC-009 decoy reported. Characterization 22/22 green.

expl_justification.clareza: States its order as priority of correction; every finding has where, mechanism, impact and fix, with severity and confidence in the header; a Decisões and a short Verificação section; the summary says up front what was and was not fixed. A few blocks run long.
expl_justification.precisao: Correct and deeper than BW/BY: the LIKE SQLi proven with payloads and the wildcards kept on purpose; visibility tested end to end before and after; PHP 8 throws on the division; three export defects in one path (fixed-name race, predictable file possibly under the web root at stated lower confidence, silent fopen failure); $escape passed explicitly for PHP 8.4 to keep the output byte-identical; verChamado/tecnicoNome correctly not exploitable; gradual MD5 migration with hash_equals. It swaps the PHP division for AVG() and calls the value the same without considering the rounded DECIMAL (77/3), and says nothing on bcrypt's 72-byte and NUL limits. It repeats both secret literals in the text (not scored separately).
expl_justification.causa_raiz: Real causes with mechanisms: the visibility rule 'is not applied anywhere'; F10 ties the int-typed concatenation to the same pattern that produced F1. No structural synthesis of the authorization gap at the K/BT/BX level.
expl_justification.priorizacao: Priority order stated and kept (2 critical, 3 high, 3 medium, 3 low) with confidence lowered where exposure depends on the vhost; effort weighed only in passing; no deployment sequencing (nothing on running the column ALTER first).
expl_justification.trade_offs: Real, argued trade-offs: the filter in the web layer so internal consumers keep everything; the CSV restricted to technicians, admitted as a visible behaviour change and defended from the manifest; MD5 kept in the seed to prove the transparent migration; Secure/SameSite left to deployment behind a TLS proxy; a strict formatarStatus judged not worth it; tempnam plus unlink over the shared file. Alternatives are named and weighed but not systematically compared, and the AVG swap is presented as free.
